title: Look Up Tonight: Shooting Stars Are Coming
summary: Tonight is a great night to look at the sky. The Leonid meteor shower is at its peak. You could see up to 15 shooting stars every hour. The best time to watch is between midnight and dawn on Tuesday. The moon will set before midnight, so the sky will be dark. Find a place far from city lights. Lie down and look up at a wide part of the sky. Wait about 20 minutes for your eyes to get used to the dark. Do not use binoculars or a telescope. They make you see only a small part of the sky. The Leonids are some of the fastest shooting stars of the year. They move at 43 miles every second. They often leave bright lines of light behind them. They come from tiny bits of dust left by a comet called Tempel-Tuttle. The comet takes 33 years to go around the sun. It last came close in 1998 and will come back in 2031.
why_it_matters: Watching shooting stars is a fun way to see space with just your eyes.
